epic.intent:
## Outcome
An agent can record a scripted browser walkthrough of a web app with webreel and attach it as evidence to an attempt or a Kanban card. The person plays the clip in the app next to the screenshots, at the checkpoint or in card review. The person can also launch a recording of a saved webreel script from the folder page.

## Confirmed decisions (person, 2026-11-12)
- Video is a new evidence attachment kind stored only in the local database. Git-tracked records carry its poster frame (a still image), its SHA-256, size, duration and dimensions. A clone or another machine sees the poster and a "video not on this machine" notice, never a broken player.
- Deep integration: the app can run a recording itself.
- Acceptance targets: the fixture web app and Dark Mechanicus's own renderer dev server.

## Evidence inspected
- webreel 0.1.4 (npm, Apache-2.0); last release 2026-03-02, repository still active in November 2026. It drives headless Chrome from a JSON config and encodes with ffmpeg; both are downloaded to `~/.webreel` on first use. Output is MP4, WebM or GIF; it can also write PNG screenshots at chosen steps.
- `docs/decisions/0006-image-attachments.md`: attachments are PNG or JPEG, 10 MiB, exported into the repository in repo mode. This epic amends that decision for video.
- Not yet verified: webreel on Windows, which codecs Electron 42 plays, and typical clip sizes. The epic starts with that investigation.

## Scope
- Video attachment kind: intake, limits, storage, poster, playback, portable metadata, strict import.
- Register webreel as a capability (requires the Capabilities epic); its Chrome and ffmpeg downloads are disclosed at install.
- A `dm` path for an agent to attach a recorded file as evidence, and a run-from-the-app action.

## Non-goals
- Video as a planner reference on tickets or cards (evidence only).
- Editing, trimming or re-encoding clips in the app.
- Recording the desktop or the Electron window itself; webreel records a URL in its own headless Chrome.
- Carrying video through a Linear transfer.
- Native verification on macOS or Linux: no such machine is available to this project today. Those code paths are unit-tested and the runbook says the feature is verified on Windows only.

## Standards
Only the project Definition of Done gates acceptance. Each ticket writes and runs the tests its Tests section lists.

successCriteria.text: An agent records the fixture web app with webreel and attaches the clip to an attempt as evidence through the dm CLI; the attempt shows a poster frame and plays the clip in the app.
In repo mode the Git-tracked records gain only the poster image and a metadata sidecar for the clip; no video bytes appear anywhere under the repository.
On a fresh reconstruction of the folder from its Git records the attempt shows the poster and a notice that the video is not on this machine, with no error.
A file that is not a supported video, is truncated, or exceeds the size or duration limit is refused before anything is stored.
The person starts a recording of a saved script from the folder page, sees it run and stop, and finds the output file path shown.
A recording of Dark Mechanicus's own renderer dev server is attached to the acceptance node as evidence.

epic.title: webreel: scripted browser recordings kept as local video evidence

bundle.rationale:
## Approach
One sprint, one deliverable (person, 2026-11-15): an agent records a web app with webreel and the clip is first-class evidence the person can play. An investigation fixes formats and limits first; intake, storage, portable records and playback make video an evidence kind; webreel registration and run-from-the-app build on the Capabilities engine; the guides and a Windows smoke close it.

## Decisions and why
- **Person's choice: bytes stay in the local database; Git carries a poster and metadata.** Keeps repositories small. Cost: a reviewer on another machine sees only the poster, so the guides tell them to ask for a re-run when the clip matters.
- **The caller supplies the poster.** `add_attachment` runs in a headless process with no browser engine, so the app cannot decode a frame there. webreel can write a PNG in the same run. Rejected: generating the poster in the renderer (not available to the headless CLI) and bundling ffmpeg in the app (size and licence).
- **Containers are measured, not decoded.** Intake reads a few header fields with hard bounds. No frame is decoded in the core process.
- **Evidence only.** A video cannot be a planner reference on a ticket or card in this epic.
- **Provisional limits: MP4 with H.264 and WebM with VP9, 50 MiB, 5 minutes.** The investigation confirms or changes them with measurements.
- **Run-from-the-app reads only a JSON script at the folder root**, as untrusted data; the output path must resolve inside the folder.

## Assumptions the investigation must confirm
- Electron 42 plays what webreel writes, from the app's custom protocol.
- webreel 0.1.4 works on Windows when installed with lifecycle scripts off. Its last release was in March 2026; if it does not work, the investigation's accepted result blocks the webreel tickets and the orchestrator escalates the scope decision to the person; the video evidence kind stands by itself.

## Risks
- Parsing hostile containers: bounded walk, mutation-loop test, deep-review capability on that ticket.
- Database growth from local video: bounded per clip and per record; the runbook says how to free space. A total cap is not planned.
- webreel downloads Chrome and ffmpeg outside the app's private folder: disclosed in the install dialog, not prevented.
- A table rebuild migration: pinned-hash test for existing records and a row-preservation test.

## Sequencing
Investigation first. Video chain: intake, storage, then portable records and playback in parallel. webreel chain: descriptor (after the investigation), then run-from-app. Guides follow storage. The smoke joins portable records, playback and run-from-app. Critical path: investigation, intake, storage, portable records, smoke.

## Dependencies on other epics
Requires the Capabilities epic complete before the run starts. The video evidence tickets do not use it, but the epic ships as one increment.

tickets.title: Sprint 1 acceptance

acceptanceCriteria.text: `docs/reports/webreel-windows.md` answers the six questions with commands, outputs, dates and versions, including measured clip sizes for both containers at both lengths.

ADR 0008 states the accepted containers and codecs, the byte and duration limits, the poster model, local-only storage, the sidecar fields and the import behaviour, each with the measurement or reason behind it.
`src/test/videos.ts` holds one small valid MP4 and one small valid WebM sample that Electron 42 plays.
Anything not established on Windows is named as unverified in the report.

tickets.body:
## Context
Attachments are PNG or JPEG, at most 10 MiB, exported into the repository in repo mode (ADR 0006). The person decided video evidence stays in the local database, with only a poster frame and metadata in Git. The exact formats and limits depend on what webreel writes and what Electron 42 plays.

## Questions to answer, each with the command, its output, the date and the version
1. Does `npm ci --ignore-scripts` from a lockfile pinned to `webreel@0.1.4` give a working `webreel`? What do `webreel install` and the first run download to `~/.webreel` (names, sizes, any published checksum)?
2. Record the fixture web app (`scripts/native/fixtures/webapp/`) as MP4 and as WebM: file sizes for a 10 second and a 60 second clip at the default viewport and at 1280 by 720; container, codec and profile of each.
3. Does Electron 42 play each file in a `<video>` element served from a custom protocol? Does seeking need range requests, and does the scheme need the `stream` privilege?
4. Can a webreel `screenshot` step write a PNG usable as the poster in the same run?
5. What does `webreel record` print while running and on failure, and which exit codes does it use?
6. Does it run on Windows without a visible desktop session?

## Decision to write
`docs/decisions/0008-video-evidence.md`, amending 0006: accepted containers and codecs; byte and duration limits; the poster model; local-only storage; the fields of the portable sidecar; what import does when the bytes are absent; evidence only, never a planner reference. Start from these provisional values and change them only with a measured reason: MP4 with H.264 and WebM with VP9; 50 MiB; 5 minutes; a video attachment names one image attachment as its poster, supplied by the caller; 20 attachments per record unchanged.
Also commit two tiny sample clips (a few kilobytes each, MP4 and WebM) as base64 in `src/test/videos.ts` for later tests.

## Safety
Read prompts before answering; no blind key presses. Record only the fixture app. Use a throwaway working folder.

## Source locations (entry points; only the sample file is added)
- `docs/decisions/0006-image-attachments.md`.
- `src/main/desktop/protocolSchemes.ts`: `registerDesktopSchemes`; `src/main/desktop/attachmentProtocol.ts`: `handleAttachmentRequest`.
- `electron.vite.config.ts`: `PROD_CSP`, `DEV_CSP` (there is no `media-src` today).
- `src/test/images.ts`, `src/test/encodedImages.ts`: how image fixtures are stored.

## Tests
None: investigation. The evidence is the report and the decision.

reasoning.rationale: Bounded investigation that ends in a format and storage decision the rest of the epic implements.

tickets.title: Decide the video evidence format from what Electron plays and webreel produces on Windows

acceptanceCriteria.text: Both sample clips are measured with the width, height and duration the investigation recorded.
Truncated files, oversized declared sizes, over-deep nesting and out-of-limit durations are each refused with a reason; tests cover each.
A mutation loop over the samples produces only domain refusals and completes within its time bound.
A file outside the allowed folders, or reached through a symlink, is refused exactly as images are.

tickets.body:
## In scope
`src/core/attachments/video.ts`:
- `inspectVideoBytes(bytes)`: return mime, width, height and duration in milliseconds, or a refusal with a reason. Recognise by content, not extension: an MP4 `ftyp` box, or an EBML header whose DocType is `webm`.
- Read only what is needed. MP4: `moov/mvhd` timescale and duration, and the first video track's `tkhd` width and height. WebM: Segment Info duration and timecode scale, and the first video track's pixel width and height.
- Bounded walk: a maximum depth, a maximum number of boxes or elements, every declared size checked against the buffer. Refuse a truncated file, a missing `moov`, a zero or absurd duration, and anything over the limits in ADR 0008.
- No frame is decoded and nothing is executed.
- `readVideoFile(path, roots, fs)`: the same allowed-folder and no-symlink rules as `readImageFile`.

## Out of scope
Storage, commands, export, playback.

## Source locations
- `src/core/attachments/intake.ts`: `inspectImageBytes`, `readImageFile`, `resolveAllowedRoots`, `isInsideImageRoot`, `MAX_IMAGE_BYTES`. Tests: `intake.test.ts`, `intake.branches.test.ts`.
- `src/test/videos.ts` from the investigation ticket; `src/test/memoryFs.ts`.
- `docs/decisions/0008-video-evidence.md`: formats and limits.

## Tests
`src/core/attachments/video.test.ts`: both samples measured correctly; truncated file; a box size larger than the file; nesting deeper than the bound; zero and huge duration; a PNG renamed to `.mp4`; a path outside the allowed folders and a symlink are refused; a loop that mutates sample bytes several thousand times never throws anything but the domain refusal and finishes within a fixed time.

## Verify
Run the test file, lint, typecheck.

reasoning.rationale: Parses untrusted binary containers in the core process; a wrong bound is a hang or memory risk and is hard to see in review.

tickets.body:
## In scope
- Migration V15: rebuild `attachments` so its checks admit the video mime types, with a nullable duration column and a nullable poster reference to another attachment row.
- `attachmentRef` and the view types gain optional duration and poster id, and `AttachmentView` gains an `available` flag (false when the bytes are absent). No defaults are added: existing records must parse unchanged and keep their hashes.
- `add_attachment` accepts a video file when a `poster` image path is given with it. The poster is staged as an ordinary image and linked. A video without a poster is refused. A video with purpose `reference` is refused.
- Claiming a video for an attempt or a Kanban attempt claims its poster with it. Pruning an unclaimed staged video prunes its poster.
- Tickets, cards and comments refuse a video id.
- `get_attachment` with `as: file` writes a video to a temp file with the right extension.
- `uploadAttachment` (desktop paste and drop) keeps refusing video in this epic.

## Out of scope
Export to Git records, import, playback.

## Source locations
- `src/core/db/migrations.ts`: `SCHEMA_VERSION`, `MIGRATIONS`; V14 created `attachments` and shows the copy, drop, rename pattern for changing a check. Test: `migrations.test.ts`.
- `src/core/schemas.ts`: `attachmentMime`, `attachmentRef`, `attachmentPurpose`, `attemptEvidenceInput`.
- `src/shared/domain/views.ts`: `AttachmentMime`, `AttachmentRef`, `AttachmentView`, `AttachmentOwnerKind`.
- `src/core/attachments/tempFile.ts`: `writeAttachmentTempFile` and its extension map.
- `src/core/services/attachments.ts`: `stageAttachmentFile`, `createStagedAttachment`, `claimAttachments`, `claimEvidenceAttachments`, `pruneStagedAttachments`, `attachmentRefOf`. Test: `attachments.test.ts`.
- `src/core/commands/attachments.ts`: `addAttachment`, `uploadAttachment`, `getAttachment`. Tests: `attachments.test.ts`, `uploadAttachment.test.ts`.
- `src/mcp/tools/attachments.ts`: `registerAttachmentTools`. Test beside it.
- `src/core/services/attempts.ts` and `src/core/services/kanban/attempts.ts`: the evidence claim sites.
- `src/core/attachments/video.ts` from the intake ticket.

## Tests
Migration 14 to 15 keeps existing rows byte for byte; a video without a poster is refused; a video as `reference` is refused; `submit_attempt` with a video id claims the video and its poster; pruning removes both; a ticket, a card and a comment each refuse a video id; the hash of an existing image-only record is unchanged (pin one).

## Verify
Run the touched test files, lint, typecheck.

reasoning.rationale: Schema migration with a table rebuild plus changes across schemas, services and two command surfaces; existing record hashes must not move.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Exporting an attempt that has a video writes the poster image and the sidecars, and no file containing the video bytes anywhere under the repository; a test lists the folder.
Importing those records on a clean database yields the video with available false and its poster present.
Each hostile sidecar case is rejected and leaves a missing reference without failing the import; tests cover each.

tickets.body:
## Context
Today every owned attachment is exported whole into the repository in repo mode. Video must not be: Git records carry the poster image (exported as any image) and a sidecar describing the video.

## In scope
- Export: for a video attachment write only its sidecar (id, SHA-256, mime, bytes, width, height, duration, poster id, label, who staged it). Never write the video bytes under the repository.
- Import: a video sidecar with no bytes creates the row with `available` false. A video file found in an attachments folder is not imported. A hostile sidecar (bad digest, out-of-limit duration or size, a poster id that does not resolve to an image of the same owner) is rejected and leaves a missing reference, as bad images do.
- Database-only folders are unaffected.

## Source locations
- `src/core/repo/paths.ts`: `ownedPaths`, `ATTACHMENT_EXTENSIONS`.
- `src/core/repo/attachmentFiles.ts`: `unexportedAttachments`, `writeAttachmentFile`, `placementOfAttachment`, `ATTACHMENT_FILE_NAME`, `ATTACHMENT_SIDECAR_NAME`. Test: `attachmentFiles.test.ts`.
- `src/core/repo/finalizer.ts`: `exportAttachmentsOf`, `exportAttachmentFile`, `writeAttachmentSidecar`. Tests: `finalizer.test.ts`, `finalizer.kanban.test.ts`.
- `src/core/repo/portable.ts`: the `attachmentSidecar` schema.
- `src/core/repo/attachmentImport.ts`: `registerEvidenceAttachments`, `restoreAttachmentFiles`, and the private folder scan and file verification. Test: `attachmentImport.test.ts`.
- `src/core/repo/importer.ts`: the call site.

## Tests
- `finalizer.test.ts`: exporting an attempt with one video writes the poster file and two sidecars and no video file.
- `attachmentImport.test.ts`: importing those records gives a video row with `available` false and a present poster; each hostile sidecar case leaves a missing reference; a stray `.mp4` in the folder is ignored.
- A round trip in database-only mode is unchanged.

## Verify
Run the touched test files, lint, typecheck.

reasoning.rationale: Changes the finalizer and the strict importer, which treat every file as untrusted.

tickets.body:
## In scope
- `dm-attachment:` serves video with range support when the investigation says seeking needs it: `206`, `Content-Range`, `Accept-Ranges`, with every range checked against the stored size. Add the `stream` scheme privilege only if the report says it is required.
- CSP: add `media-src dm-attachment:` to the production and dev policies. Nothing else is widened.
- `AttachmentGallery`: a video tile shows the poster with a play mark and the duration. Opening it shows a `<video controls preload="none">` in the lightbox; nothing autoplays. When `available` is false the tile shows the poster and the notice "This video is not on this machine", and no player.
- Keyboard: the tile opens with Enter and Space, and the lightbox closes with Escape, as images do.
The gallery's consumers need no change.

## Source locations
- `src/main/desktop/attachmentProtocol.ts`: `parseAttachmentUrl`, `handleAttachmentRequest`, `createAttachmentLookup`. Tests: `attachmentProtocol.test.ts`, `attachmentProtocol.integration.test.ts`.
- `src/main/desktop/protocolSchemes.ts`: `registerDesktopSchemes`.
- `electron.vite.config.ts`: `PROD_CSP`, `DEV_CSP`, `cspPlugin`; injected into `src/renderer/index.html`.
- `src/renderer/src/attachments/AttachmentGallery.tsx`, `attachments.css`. Test: `AttachmentGallery.test.tsx`.
- Consumers, for a visual check only: `src/renderer/src/ticket/panelTabs.tsx`, `src/renderer/src/kanban/CardActivity.tsx`.
- `docs/reports/webreel-windows.md`: answer to question 3.

## Tests
- `attachmentProtocol.test.ts`: a valid range, a suffix range, an out-of-bounds range, an unknown id, and an id of another workspace.
- `attachmentProtocol.integration.test.ts`: a sample clip is served and its bytes match.
- `AttachmentGallery.test.tsx`: video tile, lightbox player without autoplay, the missing notice, keyboard.
- A test of the CSP strings: `media-src` allows `dm-attachment:` only.

## Verify
Run the touched tests, lint, typechecks. Attach a screenshot of a playing clip in an attempt's evidence and one of the missing notice.

reasoning.rationale: Protocol range handling in main, a CSP change and a new gallery tile with a missing state.

## In scope

tickets.body:
## In scope
`scripts/native/main/webreel.smoke.ts`:
1. Dev build, isolated user data, a scratch repository in repo mode holding the fixture web app and a webreel script with a `screenshot` step.
2. Install webreel through the card (real download of the pinned package and its Chrome and ffmpeg), turn it on.
3. Agent path: from a disposable custom CLI chat, run `webreel record`, then `add_attachment` with the clip and poster, then submit them as evidence on a scratch Kanban card through the sanctioned `dm` commands.
4. In the app, open the card's attempt, capture the poster tile and the playing clip.
